transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I've been really struggling at work lately because I keep making careless mistakes and missing important details. No matter how hard I try to focus, I just seem to overlook the small things.
Have these attention and careless-mistake problems been present since childhood or school years, or did they start more recently?

Honestly, they've been happening for as long as I can remember, definitely since I was a kid in elementary school. My teachers used to always point out that I made careless mistakes on my homework even back then. It's definitely not something that just started recently.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation), Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder], but the patient reports inattentive symptoms and careless mistakes since childhood, which strongly supports ADHD and makes GAD or MDD less likely as primary explanations because those typically do not begin in elementary school and persist in this pattern from childhood.

inference_history.note: No previous candidates were provided, so this is the initial differential based on the limited interview. The patient reports persistent careless mistakes, missed details, and difficulty sustaining focus at work, which most strongly suggests ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. Generalized Anxiety Disorder remains possible if worry is driving distractibility, and Major Depressive Disorder remains possible if low concentration is part of a depressive syndrome. There is not enough information yet to support hyperactive/impulsive symptoms, psychosis, mania, or other listed conditions.
